analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.disclaimer: The results are statistical hints based on your own entries and not a diagnosis. Talk to a doctor if you have symptoms.

summary.censored_other: {{count}} entries are too recent to be evaluated.

suspects.title: Possible intolerances
suspects.name: Name
suspects.hint: The risk factor compares how often complaints followed an ingredient with meals without it. A factor of 2 means twice as often. The interval shows the uncertainty.

charts.heatmap: Complaints by weekday and time of day

context.title: Sleep and stress
context.hint: This compares days with a complaint on days with short sleep (under 6 hours), poor sleep (rated 1 or 2) or high stress (level 4 or 5) against other days that you logged. It only uses finished days. A factor of 2 means complaints were twice as common. This shows an association, not a cause.
context.notEnough: Not enough data yet: at least {{days}} days with and {{days}} days without the factor, plus a few days with a complaint.

report.title: Foodlog report
report.method: Every meal and drink counts as an occasion. It is flagged if a complaint was logged within the time window afterwards. The risk factor compares meals with and without the respective ingredient. Ingredients with fewer than {{exposures}} meals or {{outcomes}} complaints are not rated. Ingredients that were always eaten together cannot be told apart.

ai.title: AI analysis
ai.intro: Have an AI model summarise and put your analysis into context. You need your own API key from Anthropic or OpenAI. Usage is billed to your key by the provider.
ai.disclaimer: An AI answer is not medical advice and can contain mistakes. Talk to a doctor about symptoms.

provider.title: Provider and key
provider.keyHint: The key is stored encrypted and never shown again. It is checked with the provider when you save it.

consent.title: Consent for the analysis
consent.text: When you start the analysis, your health data (entries of the selected period including sleep and stress if you track them, and the statistical pre-analysis, without name, email and notes) is sent to the selected provider and processed there. This is special category data under Art. 9 GDPR. The provider's privacy policy applies in addition. You can withdraw your consent at any time.
consent.checkbox: I consent to this data being sent to the selected provider when I start the AI analysis.

photoConsent.title: Consent for photos
photoConsent.text: When you use photo recognition, the photo you choose is sent to the selected provider and analysed there. It is reduced in size and stripped of metadata such as the location before it is sent, and it is not stored by Foodlog I/O. A photo can show more than you intend, for example people or documents. The provider's privacy policy applies in addition. You can withdraw your consent at any time.
photoConsent.checkbox: I consent to photos I choose being sent to the selected provider when I use photo recognition.

landing.title: Find out what your body does not like
landing.lead: Foodlog I/O is a diary for food, complaints and digestion. It shows which ingredients often come before your symptoms, so you have something concrete to talk about with your doctor.

points.one: Log meals, drinks, symptoms, stool, medication, sleep and stress on one timeline.
points.two: See possible triggers with an honest note on how reliable they are.
points.three: Print a report or export your data whenever you want.

landing.inviteOnly: Registration is currently by invitation only.

log.title: Write it down
log.text: Add entries in a few taps. Pick ingredients from a catalog, scan a barcode or reuse a favorite.

find.title: Look for patterns
find.text: After a few weeks the analysis compares meals that were followed by complaints with those that were not.

share.title: Talk to your doctor
share.text: A printable report and a CSV export summarise your diary and the findings.

timeline.title: One timeline
timeline.text: Meals, drinks, symptoms, stool (Bristol scale), medication, sleep and stress, with freely editable times.

ingredients.title: Ingredients and allergens
ingredients.text: A catalog with allergen categories plus your own tags. Barcode lookup fills in ingredients for packaged food.

analysis.title: Possible triggers
analysis.text: Risk ratios with a confidence interval, only shown when there is enough data, and never as a diagnosis.

context.title: Sleep and stress
context.text: Checks whether bad nights or stressful days go along with more complaints, independent of food.

report.title: Report and export
report.text: A printable report for your appointment, a CSV export and a full data export at any time.

ai.title: Optional AI analysis
ai.text: If you want a second opinion, connect your own Anthropic or OpenAI key. It is off unless you turn it on and you see exactly what is sent.

dashboard.alt: The daily timeline with a meal, a drink, a symptom, a stool entry and a medication
dashboard.caption: The day at a glance

analysis.alt: The analysis page with a chart of complaints per day and a table of possible triggers
analysis.caption: Possible triggers with their reliability

report.alt: The printable report for a doctor
report.caption: A report you can take to your appointment

trust.data: You can export or delete all of your data in your profile.
trust.open: The code is open source (AGPL), so you can check what it does or run it yourself.
trust.hint: Foodlog I/O gives hints, not diagnoses. It does not replace medical advice.
